messages:
Maya: Quick thought: instead of always sampling traffic into a deep bench, what if we do canary-first onboarding? small real-customer canaries + local golden checks -> only escalate to bench on signal. less synthetic load.
Samir: canary-first sounds good. what's the canary size and signal threshold?
Maya: propose 0.5% traffic for 1 hour, metric triggers: latency p95 > SLO*1.15 OR quality delta > 1.5% on per-customer golden. if triggered, promote to bench workflow.
Eli: how do we pick per-customer golden? don't want bias from narrow prompts.
Priya: keep golden per-tenant stratified by intent bucket and seqlen. we already have per-customer prompt clusters from analytics. use top-10 clusters + a few random tails.
Ben: operational risk: a noisy tenant could constantly flip the model. need cooldowns and circuit breakers.
Maya: agreed: add cooldown of 6h post-fallback, and noise-robust detector (median vs mean). also a hysteresis window for repeated passes.
intake-bot: [automated] bench cluster headroom: 64 workers free; token budget remaining this hour: 1.2M.
Samir: ok that helps. For escalation, bench should run stratified microbench (seqlen slices) not full golden set. less tokens but enough signal.
Eli: I'll add a new intake flag: "canary_then_bench": {"canary_pct":0.005, "escalate_on": ["latency", "quality"], "bench_mode":"microstrat"}.
Priya: plus an opt-in label to tie this to customer SLA tier. Premium customers get bigger canaries and dedicated short benches.
Ben: fallback ordering question: do we attempt quantized variant first or shorter ctx? shorter ctx might silently reduce quality. quantized is cheaper but riskier for hallucination.
Maya: propose order: 1) shorter_ctx (transparent to caller with warning header), 2) quantized_variant (internal), 3) micro-fallback-model. shorter_ctx first because it's predictable. quantized second because we can flag outputs.
Samir: let's emit metadata tags on fallback responses so consumers can decide. also rate-limit how often a customer sees fallback types.
Eli: added: responses get headers: x-onboard-fallback=[shorter_ctx|quantized|micro-model]; also a per-tenant fallback_quota.
Priya: golden drift detection: run rolling champion-challenger comparisons with KL drift + task-specific score. if drift detected, trigger retrain/golden refresh job.
Maya: note: golden refreshes must be human-reviewed for privacy-sensitive tenants. mark those in metadata.
Ben: edge case: adversarial prompt shapes causing false regressions. we should add an adversarial filter to the canary checks.
Samir: include an adversarial score and drop top outliers from signal.
intake-bot: [automated] logging note: canary events will be sampled at 100% for 24h, then 10%.
Maya: cool. action items: Samir -> controller logic (cooldowns + circuit), Eli -> intake feature + fallback headers, Priya -> golden selection stratifier + privacy labels, Ben -> adversarial filter doc. I'll open a lightweight RFC and tag @infra for bench headroom policy. Thanks all.
